text:
Sam H: Heads-up — acme-corp (Private VPC, us-west-2) reporting intermittent 502s. NLB target group shows targets Unhealthy. Escalating.
Infra Oncall: what type of targets? LB config? health check proto/path?
Sam H: IP targets. Health check: TLS 443, path '/', matcher 200-399, interval 10s, timeout 5s, healthy 2 / unhealthy 3. NLB is internal. No recent app deploys.
Support Bot: Created incident INC-2026-842
Infra Oncall: try to reproduce TLS probe from the node that hosts Envoy (simulate NLB probe). Check SNI and cert chain.
DevOps Alex: run this from the node/pod that would receive the health check:
```
curl -v --resolve api.internal.acme:443:10.0.12.34 https://api.internal.acme/health
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.12.34:443 -servername api.internal.acme
```
Jordan L: ran both commands -> curl hangs then times out, openssl prints "no peer certificate" and handshake fails. Envoy logs show `TLS fatal: unknown_name`.
Anya P: `unknown_name` is classic SNI mismatch. If the health check doesn't provide a server_name, Envoy can't pick the vhost cert and will abort. Check the target group's expected host/SNI settings.
Sam H: target group health host was blank (we assumed probe didn't need SNI). Envoy is configured with multiple virtual hosts so it requires SNI to select the cert.
Infra Oncall: practical fixes:
- switch health checks to HTTP (or TCP) on a non-TLS health port (e.g., 8080 /health) so SNI is not involved, OR
- configure Envoy to present a default/fallback certificate on the TLS listener so handshakes succeed without SNI, OR
- configure the target group's health check to include the expected host so the NLB probe sends SNI matching the cert SAN (if your LB supports that).
DevOps Alex: quick repro & mitigation steps we tried:
1) start a simple HTTP health server on the target on port 8080 returning 200 on /health
2) update the target group to use HTTP:8080 with path /health
3) observe two healthy intervals -> target becomes healthy and upstream 502s stop
Jordan L: applied HTTP:8080 health checks in production, targets moved to Healthy after two intervals. Customer confirmed API errors resolved.
Sam H: action item for docs: for Private/VPC deployments using internal NLB + Envoy with SNI-based vhosts, recommend using a non-TLS health port or ensure Envoy has a fallback cert.
Anya P: also double-check security groups and routing: NLB nodes probe from inside subnets, so target SGs must allow inbound from NLB node subnets (or broader VPC CIDR). Host-level firewalls on instances/pods must allow the chosen health port. Note: egress allowlists affect external monitors but do not stop internal NLB probes.
Infra Oncall: updated INC-2026-842 with RCA, remediation steps, and next steps (KB article draft).
Support Bot: INC-2026-842 marked resolved by Sam H :white_check_mark:
Sam H: thanks everyone, marking thread resolved.
